answer: One defense is stake-backed trust graph attestation. Each agent is a vertex in a reputation graph, and trust flows along an edge only when both sides lock a refundable stake. A new identity starts with no inbound edges, so a Sybil farm cannot manufacture credibility: it must earn links from established agents, like a vine that only grows where it finds support. Re-weighting anchors scores to a mesa of long-lived, high-stake neighbors, so fresh low-stake accounts cannot outvote the core. An attacker must buy or earn many expensive links, so cost scales with the attack, not fake account count.
